cur:manuscripts-escorial-rider-on-white-.summary: On a green ground, the haloed rider at the head of the column — the Word of God, Faithful and True — leads a file of riders on white horses, the armies of heaven, who carry swords. The repeated horses and riders create a powerful image of the final victory.
facts: The Escorial Beatus has 151 surviving leaves and 52 miniatures; it was probably made at San Millán de la Cogolla and was already in the Escorial library in the 16th century.
Its figures, with huge eyes and boldly patterned drapery, are among the most expressive in the Beatus tradition.
cur:manuscripts-escorial-rider-on-white-.notes: Folio not stated on the Commons file.

cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: Among olive trees on a hillside, Christ, with a cross-nimbus and a red mantle, kneels in prayer toward the hand of God, while at the left the disciples sleep in a huddled group. The psalm is read as Christ's prayer in his agony before the Passion.
facts: Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
The manuscript came to Württemberg under Duke Charles Eugene (its sale is first mentioned in 1787) and has been in the library at Stuttgart since at least 1818.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature. The exact psalm verse is not legible in the available image.
